n: Right after describing Israel’s judgment (43:28), God says, “But now listen.” Judgment is not His last word; His chosen servant still has a future.
The Lord who formed Israel from the womb promises help and says again, “Fear not.” He uses the affectionate name Jeshurun, “upright one”—a name expressing what Israel was meant to be.

f.g: Jeshurun, “the upright one,” a poetic pet name for Israel.

n: Like rain on parched ground, God will pour out His Spirit on Israel’s children. Joel later uses similar language, and Latter-day Saints see it fulfilled in the Restoration.

f.w: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed

n: Their descendants will flourish like grass and like willows along streams—fresh, green, and growing.

f.w: as willows by the water courses

n: People will proudly claim the Lord: one says “I belong to the Lord,” another writes “the Lord’s” on his hand. Even outsiders may join Israel by covenant—a picture of conversion and adoption.

f.w: subscribe with his hand unto the LORD
f.g: Write on his hand “belonging to the Lord,” like a mark of ownership or loyalty.

f.w: surname himself by the name of Israel

n: The Lord is Israel’s King and Redeemer, the First and the Last; there is no other God. The resurrected Christ uses this title for Himself in Revelation.

f.w: I am the first, and I am the last

n: Who else can announce the future and lay it out in order as God has done since ancient times? Let the idols try.

f.g: Literally “the everlasting people”—the people of long ago.

n: Don’t be afraid—God told you long ago, and you are His witnesses. Is there any other God? He knows of no other Rock.

f.g: The Hebrew adds “no Rock”—God as the stable foundation.

n: A long satire begins. Idol makers are empty, and the treasured idols they love are useless. Their gods can’t see or know anything—an embarrassing witness for them.

f.g: Things they delight in—their prized idols.

n: Who would make a god that profits nothing?
Everyone involved will be ashamed. The craftsmen are only humans; let them gather and see how they tremble together.
The blacksmith sweats at the forge, hammering the idol with all his strength until he’s hungry, thirsty, and exhausted. The god he makes can’t even give him a drink of water.

f.g: Or a cutting tool used in metalwork.

n: The carpenter measures, marks, and planes wood into a handsome human shape—to sit in a house. The idol is shaped like a man and can do even less than one.

f.g: A tool for drawing curves and circles.

n: He cuts down cedar, cypress, or oak, or plants a tree and waits for rain to grow it. Notice: it is God’s rain that grows the wood for the idol.

f.g: Probably a laurel or pine; the exact tree is uncertain.

n: The same wood is firewood: he warms himself and bakes bread with it—then makes a god from it and bows down to it.
Half of it he burns, cooks meat over it, eats his fill, and says, “Ah, I’m warm!”
And from the leftover piece he makes a god, bows down, and prays, “Save me, you are my god!” Isaiah’s humor exposes how absurd it is to worship what we make.

f.w: Deliver me; for thou art my god

n: They don’t understand because their eyes are smeared shut and their hearts closed. Idolatry blinds.
No one stops to think, “I baked bread on half of this—should I bow down to the other half, a block of wood?”

f.g: A block or chunk of wood.

n: Such a person feeds on ashes. A deceived heart leads him astray so he can’t save himself or admit, “This thing in my hand is a lie.” Modern idols—money, status, pleasure—can blind in the same way.

f.w: Is there not a lie in my right hand?

n: Remember this, Israel: you are My servant whom I formed. I will never forget you.

f.w: thou shalt not be forgotten of me

n: God has swept away Israel’s sins like a morning mist that the sun burns off. Forgiveness is already offered; the invitation is “Return to Me.”

f.w: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions
return unto me; for I have redeemed thee

n: All creation is invited to sing—heavens, depths, mountains, forests—because the Lord has redeemed Jacob and shown His glory in Israel.
The Redeemer who formed Israel is also the Maker of everything, who alone stretched out the heavens and spread out the earth.

f.w: I am the LORD that maketh all things

n: He frustrates false prophets and fortune-tellers and turns the “wisdom” of the world into foolishness.

f.g: Omens or signs used by diviners.

n: But He fulfills the words of His true servants and messengers. He declares that Jerusalem will be lived in again and Judah’s ruined towns rebuilt.

f.w: confirmeth the word of his servant

n: He can command even the deep waters to dry up—recalling the Red Sea, and perhaps hinting at Babylon’s river defenses.

f.w: I will dry up thy rivers

n: Remarkably, God names Cyrus as His shepherd who will order Jerusalem and the temple rebuilt. Cyrus of Persia did issue such a decree in 538 BC. Many scholars date this passage to the exile; Latter-day Saints see it as genuine prophecy by Isaiah long before Cyrus lived.

f.g: “Shepherd” was a common ancient title for a king.
